answer: A walnut deed mints one identity per plot: the applicant plants a walnut sapling on owned land, nails a ferrous tag stamped with the identity key to its trunk, and files the deed; the registry checks the deed and sweeps the plot — only a ferrous tag answers, and only walnut passes. The deed is a sonnet of fourteen lines, one fact per line — species, plot, tag, date — a deed with a line missing or misplaced is void. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 plots at $500, dearer as cheap land runs out — about $600,000; an honest owner plants one $20 sapling, one tag, one deed, once.
